result.summary: Adds an evalscript subcommand to bitcoin-util that runs the real consensus script interpreter over a user-supplied script and stack, optionally with a transaction and spent outputs to validate signatures and locktime opcodes. To support this it extracts CastToBool and a new CheckTapscriptOpSuccess helper from script/interpreter.cpp/h without changing their behavior, and adds functional tests covering various sigversions, flags, and OP_SUCCESS handling.
result.problem: Developers and reviewers working on script/consensus changes currently have no lightweight way to evaluate a script fragment against real consensus logic; they must construct full transactions or rely on external tooling (the PR notes this was previously carried in the bitcoin-inquisition fork). This tool gives them a fast, direct way to inspect script execution, signature checks, and OP_SUCCESS behavior.

Whether jeanpablojp's test-coverage suggestion will be treated as material enough to warrant a follow-up before merge is unclear given no author response yet, though the 55-day silence has not yet crossed the 60-day stale threshold.
result.card: This PR adds an evalscript subcommand to bitcoin-util, letting developers run a script and stack through Bitcoin Core's real consensus interpreter for debugging, previously carried in the bitcoin-inquisition fork. It makes a mechanical extraction of two functions (CastToBool, CheckTapscriptOpSuccess) from script/interpreter.cpp with no stated consensus behavior change, plus functional tests for the new command. A single reviewer (jeanpablojp) gave a tested ACK after running the unit tests and feature_taproot, with only a non-blocking suggestion to add test coverage for the untested -tx signature-validation path. The PR is otherwise mergeable and not blocked; the author has been silent since opening it but the outstanding comment is minor. Priority is moderate as a developer tool (tools) and low as a validation change since it doesn't alter consensus logic.
